stem: An African child is found to have a mass in the jaw. A biopsy of the mass was done, and it appears as shown in the image below. The child also had a translocation of t(8;14). What is the probable diagnosis?
explanation: A jaw mass in an African child with a starry-sky appearance on biopsy and t(8;14) (c-MYC translocation) is endemic Burkitt lymphoma, associated with EBV.

stem: An infant presents with hepatosplenomegaly and thrombocytopenia. Neuroimaging with CT shows periventricular calcifications. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Hepatosplenomegaly, thrombocytopenia and periventricular calcifications on CT in an infant indicates congenital cytomegalovirus infection. Toxoplasmosis shows diffuse calcifications.

stem: The temperature of a body of a deceased person is found to be 39 degrees Celsius. Which of the following is the most probable reason?
explanation: A raised body temperature in a dead body (postmortem caloricity) occurs in septicaemia, heat stroke, tetanus and conditions with high pre-mortem fever, because bacterial or muscular activity continues to generate heat.

stem: A child presented to the hospital with cola-colored urine, hypertension, and puffiness of eyes. Laboratory investigations were done, and creatinine was 2.5 mg/dL. Treatment was started, and despite treatment, the patient did not improve for the next 3 weeks. The creatinine value increased to 4.5 mg/dL. Which among the following electron microscopic findings will be seen in this patient?
explanation: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis presents with cola-coloured urine, hypertension and puffiness. Electron microscopy shows subepithelial humps and immunofluorescence shows granular IgG and C3 deposits.

stem: A 35-year-old homeless man presented with a 1-month history of fever, cough, and weight loss. Both sputum smears turned out to be negative, but the chest x-ray ordered was suggestive of tuberculosis. According to the recent NTEP guidelines, which is the next best line of management?
options: Wait until TB culture results to start ATT
explanation: A symptomatic person with a chest X-ray suggestive of TB and negative sputum smears should have a CBNAAT (GeneXpert) test, which detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance within hours. Culture takes weeks.

stem: A farmer was sleeping in the field, and he felt a sting on his leg. He saw something moving away quickly. He then got drowsy and was taken to the hospital. He developed pain around the site and continued to bleed profusely from the wound site. The wound became red with blisters. Which of the following is the most likely cause?
explanation: A farmer who is stung at night during sleep by a snake and develops local pain and swelling, drowsiness and bleeding most likely was bitten by a viper. Cobra bites are mainly neurotoxic, with little local pain.

stem: A patient was transfused 4 units of blood 2 hours ago, and now she complains of chest discomfort. X-ray shows bilateral fissural thickening. Which of the following is the most probable cause?
explanation: Chest discomfort and bilateral fissural thickening/pulmonary oedema within hours of transfusion of several units is transfusion-associated circulatory overload (fluid overload), especially in the elderly and cardiac patients.

stem: Which of the following is the sensitive indicator to assess the availability, utilization, and effectiveness of healthcare in a community?
explanation: The infant mortality rate is a sensitive indicator of the availability, utilisation and effectiveness of health care in a community, as well as socio-economic development.

stem: A 48-year-old man presents with complaints of facial puffiness, frothy urine, and hypertension. He gives a history of infection with hepatitis B. Urine examination reveals microscopic hematuria. The histopathological image of the kidney biopsy shows a spike and dome pattern. What is the diagnosis of this condition?
explanation: An adult with nephrotic syndrome and hepatitis B has membranous nephropathy, with subepithelial deposits and spikes on silver stain. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C, malignancy and drugs are secondary causes.

stem: A 5-year-old child is brought with fever, fatigue, and left ventricular dysfunction. An endomyocardial biopsy is shown below. What is the probable diagnosis?
explanation: Fever, fatigue and left ventricular dysfunction in a child with an endomyocardial biopsy showing lymphocytic infiltrate and myocyte injury is lymphocytic (viral) myocarditis, commonly due to coxsackievirus B.

stem: An elderly male is known as a smoker presented with chronic cough, significant weight loss, and fatigue. Serum calcium level is raised. A lung biopsy was done, and it showed large atypical cells with hyperchromasia. What is the probable diagnosis?
explanation: A smoker with cough, weight loss and raised serum calcium (PTHrP secretion) with large atypical cells with keratin pearls is squamous cell carcinoma of the lung, a centrally located tumour associated with hypercalcaemia.

stem: An elderly male went for a medical examination. Laboratory investigations showed a marked elevation of lymphocytes with marked leukocytosis. The peripheral smear of the patient is given below. What is the appropriate next step for this patient?
explanation: Marked lymphocytosis in an elderly man with smudge cells on a smear suggests chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. Flow cytometry (CD5, CD19, CD23 positive) confirms the diagnosis.

stem: A 25-year-old male presented with low hemoglobin, platelet count of 25,000/mL, gum bleeding, and raised PT & aPTT. The image of his peripheral smear is given below. What is the likely diagnosis?
explanation: Pancytopenia with bleeding, prolonged PT and aPTT (DIC) and a smear with abnormal promyelocytes with Auer rods (faggot cells) is acute promyelocytic leukaemia, AML with t(15;17) (PML-RARA). Treat with ATRA.

stem: A young patient presents with a large retroperitoneal hemorrhage. He also gives a frequent history of intermittent swelling of knees on strenuous exercise. There is no history of any mucosal bleeding. Which among the following clotting factors is responsible for the condition mentioned above?
explanation: Spontaneous large bleeds into muscle or retroperitoneum and haemarthrosis, with no mucosal bleeding and prolonged aPTT, indicates haemophilia (factor VIII or IX deficiency). von Willebrand disease causes mucosal bleeding.

stem: A chronic smoker who worked in a cement factory for 20 years developed mesothelioma. The association is likely to be due to ________.
explanation: Malignant mesothelioma is strongly associated with asbestos exposure; asbestosis, lung cancer and mesothelioma are the major diseases. Cement factories historically used asbestos in cement sheets.

stem: The average daily dietary nutrient intake level sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of nearly all (97-98%) healthy individuals in a particular life stage and gender group is known as?
explanation: The Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) is the average daily intake that meets the requirement of 97-98% of healthy individuals in a group (EAR plus 2 SD). EAR meets the needs of 50%.
